newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar heads lower in May's last session.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar heads lower in May's last session.

text.p: Activity was more subdued on London's white sugar market during the last session before May's expiry with a confused nearby structure and tight price movements, traders said on Tuesday.

Apart from the usual position-rolling before the spot position goes off the board at close of business, light fund interest was noted in second-month August and all traded months drifted gently lower.
The nearby May/August spread remained at a discount while August/October was at a premium.
"It's all over the place -- I think you'd find it hard to get a value on the spread. They're so wide apart," said one trader.
At 1145 GMT May was down 70 cents at $305.80 and August down 80 cents at $308.10. Volume was roughly spread between May and August and amounted to 820 lots.
Another talking point in the market was the amount of sugar expected to be delivered against May, especially the likely extent of long positions.
Traders have said anything between two and 10 cargoes could be delivered from European ports.
In other news, Russia is to levy a 25 percent duty on all white sugar imports from May 15 but the tariff will not apply to Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, which have a customs treaty with Russia.
The tariff is to be no lower than 0.07 ECUS per kg.
Sri Lanka bought 12,500 tonnes of Mexican white sugar at $337.98 per tonne c & f, with delivery set for the first half of June in Colombo.
Paris turnover was dominated by trades in spot May, which also expires on Tuesday, and totalled 751 lots.
May was down $2.50 at $306.50 and August down 30 cents at $308.00.
